passages.title: Text A
text: My name is Sofia. I was born in Lisbon in 1990, but when I was seven, my family moved to Manchester, so I grew up in the UK.
Now I'm a hairdresser, and I work in a small salon in the city centre.
I usually start work at nine and finish at six, but on Saturdays I finish earlier, at three.
My husband is a mechanic, and he works for a big company just outside the city.
We've got two children — a son, who is ten, and a daughter, who is six.
Our daughter can already swim really well, better than most children her age!
Every evening, we have dinner together, and then the children usually watch a cartoon before bed.
Last month, we went to Portugal to visit my parents.
It was wonderful to see them again, and the weather there was much warmer than in Manchester.
We've never had a proper family holiday before, so it felt very special.

questions.prompt: Sofia grew up in Portugal.
She works as a hairdresser.
Her daughter can swim better than most children her age.
The family often goes on holiday together.
Why did the family go to Portugal last month?

passages.title: Text B
text: Hi, I'm Marek. I've lived in Warsaw all my life, and I work as a photographer for a small magazine.
I don't have a typical nine-to-five job — some days I start very early, and other days I don't work until the evening.
I love my job because every day is different, and I've met a lot of interesting people through my work.
Last year, I travelled to Iceland to take photos of the mountains and the sea.
It was colder than I expected, but the views were more beautiful than anything I'd seen before.
I've never been somewhere so quiet.
This year, I'm going to visit Japan in the autumn, because I'd like to photograph the autumn colours there.
Before the trip, I need to save some money, so at the moment I'm working extra hours at the weekend.
My friends think I should relax more, but I really enjoy staying busy.
Have you ever visited a place that changed the way you see the world? Iceland did that for me.

He travelled to Iceland last year.
Iceland was warmer than Marek expected.
Marek is going to visit Japan next year.
Why is Marek working extra hours at the weekend?
options: He needs to save money for his trip

lines.t: Wow! Look at all this different food!
I know. I can't decide what I want.
Well there's some pizza over there.
No! We can have pizza any day. Let's try something different.
It's Kung Pao chicken.
It smells so good! What does it come with?
It comes with some noodles.
I don't really like noodles. Is there any bread?
No, we don't have any bread, sorry. But we have some rice.
Great. So could I have a small Kung Pao chicken with some rice, please?
And the same for me, but I'd like some noodles, please.
OK, and would you like any drinks?
Can I have a bottle of lemonade?
We don't have any bottles of lemonade, I'm afraid. We have Coke or water.
OK. Well, just a Coke, please.
And for me, too.

lines.t: So, how are the plans for this year's Mandela Day?
Great, thanks! We're getting emails from people all around the world telling us how they're going to celebrate the day.
That's good to hear. So what is everyone going to do?

Oh, all sorts of things. A lot of people are going to make soup and sandwiches and give them to homeless people. I had an email from a man yesterday — he isn't going to eat for 24 hours and he's going to collect money for his local hospital.
Are you going to have time to do something yourself?
No, I'm afraid I'm not going to have much time at all. But we are going to have a big party here at the office and everyone needs to buy a ticket to come.

questions.prompt: What are a lot of people going to do for Mandela Day?
options: Make soup and sandwiches for homeless people

questions.prompt: What is the man in the email going to do?
options: Not eat for 24 hours and collect money for a hospital

lines.t: Nobuyuki Tsujii was born blind, but he started playing on a toy piano at the age of just two.
He began learning the piano two years later, and he gave his first big concert in Tokyo when he was twelve years old.
He's in his twenties now, but he has given concerts all over the world, and he has won many prizes and international competitions.
He hasn't seen the written music, but he has learnt to play some of the most difficult pieces of music in the world only through sound.

grammar.en: Go back through the grammar stage of Lessons 1–31 — focus especially on Past Simple vs Present Perfect, comparatives/superlatives, and should/have to.
grammar.ru: Вернитесь к грамматике уроков 1–31 — особенно Past Simple и Present Perfect, сравнительная и превосходная степень, should/have to.
grammar.kk: 1–31-сабақтардың грамматикасына оралыңыз — әсіресе Past Simple мен Present Perfect, салыстырмалы және күшейтпелі шырай, should/have to.

vocabulary.en: Revisit the flashcards across units — family, jobs, clothes, kitchen items and directions vocabulary come up again and again.
vocabulary.ru: Повторите карточки по всем юнитам — семья, профессии, одежда, кухонные предметы и направления встречаются снова и снова.

reading.en: Re-read the reading-led lessons (they're written specially for this course, not from the coursebook), and practise picking out the key fact rather than every word.

reading.kk: Оқылымға арналған сабақтарды қайта оқыңыз (мәтіндер осы курсқа арнайы жазылған, оқулықта жоқ) және әр сөзді емес, негізгі фактіні табуға жаттығыңыз.

listening.en: Replay the Listening tracks around Units 9–12 (food/quantities, comparatives, future plans, present perfect) — listen for the answer, not for every word.
